information_for_contributors: Aontu — published grammar (TextMate), for SYNTAX HIGHLIGHTING.
The third consumer of the published surface, beside grammar/aontu.gbnf
and grammar/aontu.lark: those two constrain a decoder, this one colours
a reader. One file serves every TextMate host — the VS Code extension
(editors/vscode), Shiki on aontu.dev, and GitHub's Linguist if and when
`.aon` clears its usage bar — so a scope added here reaches all of them.
It is a HIGHLIGHTER, not a parser: it accepts more than the language
does, and is meant to. A file mid-edit must still colour, so nothing
here refuses. What it must never do is colour a spelling the engine
rejects AS THOUGH it were valid, which is why the builtin list below is
the engine's own set and not a hand-picked sample of it.
THE BUILTIN LIST IS A COPY, AND A COPY DRIFTS. aontu.lark carried
`same` — never a builtin — and was missing `acyclic`, `inverse` and
`rel` for two releases, with every test green. So the same guard the
other two grammars have covers this file: ts/test/grammar.test.ts,
`the-textmate-grammar-names-exactly-the-engine-builtins`, asserts this
list against BUILTIN_FUNCS in BOTH directions. Add a builtin to the
engine without adding it here and that test fails.
No `|>`: ADR-018 removed the pipe from the language, and all three
published grammars now agree about that.
name: aontu

include-directive.comment: @"path" pulls in another source. The engine's only import.

key.comment: A map entry's key, bare or quoted, with the optional marker. Listed BEFORE #string so a quoted key does not read as a string, and before #kind so `string: 1` colours `string` as the key it is. Chained keys (`a: b: c: 1`) each match in turn.

spread.comment: `&: value` — the map-wide template, distinct from `&` the conjunct.

builtin.comment: The engine's function registry. `func: name "(" ...` in aontu.lark — only these names can be called, so a call to anything else is deliberately left uncoloured rather than dressed up as valid. The prefix family is spelled longest-first (refer|rel|rem|re) to keep the intent legible; the trailing \b already makes the order immaterial, since a short alternative that swallowed the stem fails the boundary and backtracks.

kind.comment: Scalar kinds. `number` is the numeric supertype; the rest of the numerics are its leaves.
kind.name: support.type.builtin.aontu

patterns.comment: `_` is a literal of the language as of G8 phase 3, not text.
patterns.name: constant.language.placeholder.aontu

reference.comment: `$.a.b` resolves from the document root; `.a.b` names a sibling, resolved against the enclosing map. Canon emits the relative form wherever a spread template survives unresolved, so both are real. No conflict with a number: a numeric literal always starts with a digit or `-`, so it matches at an earlier offset and wins there.

patterns.comment: The exact decimal — `0d19.99`. MUST precede the ordinary number: both start at the same `0`, and at equal offsets the first listed pattern wins, so the other order colours the `0` alone and leaves `d19.99` bare.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.exact.aontu
